transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
Any time I have to get blood drawn, I go to great lengths to avoid it or sit there in sheer terror the whole time. It has just become such a terrible ordeal, and I don't know what to do anymore.
Does this intense fear only happen when you are facing blood draws or needles, or do you also experience sudden panic attacks that seem to come out of nowhere?

No, it never happens out of the blue. These terrible feelings—like my heart pounding and feeling light-headed—only happen when I have to face a blood draw, see a needle, or even look at a picture of one. It is entirely focused on those medical procedures.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear of blood draws and needles?
This has been going on for close to a year now. It all started right after that routine blood test where I fainted and ended up breaking my wrist.
Since that incident, do you experience distressing nightmares or sudden flashbacks where you feel like you are re-living the moment you fainted and broke your wrist?

No, I don't experience any nightmares or flashbacks about the fall at all. I don't re-live it in my sleep or during the day; the terror only hits me when I actually have to face getting my blood drawn.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a marked, persistent, and disproportionate fear of blood draws and needles (blood-injection-injury phobia) that has lasted for nearly a year. The symptoms (heart pounding, light-headedness, sheer terror) are exclusively triggered by exposure to or anticipation of the phobic stimulus, with active avoidance of these situations. There is no evidence of panic disorder (no unexpected panic attacks) or PTSD (no nightmares or flashbacks following the initiating event).
